messages.subject: HMC samplers stuck with ZIP
parts:
I've had a recent problem getting zero-inflated Poisson models to run using HMC samplers on several different ZIP models. I've tried a few modifications with no luck. The chains are stuck at initial values unless I change the parameters samplers to RW, then sampling works. Is this a software limitation or is there anything else I can try to get this working? I could really use the speed up in convergence.

Things I've tried:
(1) Using the ZIP distribution function provided on the nimble help docs here:
https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/zero_inflated_poisson.html
and the latent parameterization. 
(2) Changing the HMC samplers to RW samplers for various parameters. 

I realize this is not a reproducible example, but it's happened every time I've tried to use a ZIP model. I can provide code if needed for troubleshooting, but I wanted to check that it's not something obvious first. 

Nimble has been an extremely useful tool for my work, so I appreciate all the work and developement going into this package. 
Cheers,
Brian

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: HMC samplers stuck with ZIP
parts:
Dear Brian,

 

If the ZIP is parameterized as a Bernoulli-Poisson mixture, then it has a binary, i.e., discrete, random effect coming from the Bernoulli. Those can’t be done with HMC; same with Stan as well.

 

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: HMC samplers stuck with ZIP
parts:
Hi Marc and others,
Thanks for the response. I'm aware of the limitation of using HMC on discrete random effects from the Bernoulli. I was hoping that changing those samplers, specifically those associated with the Bernoulli parameters, would allow the model to work with HMC sampling the other parameters, but that hasn't seemed to work. Does this mean any ZIP model will simply not work using a combination of HMC (on lambda params) and random walk (on bernoulli params) samplers? I want to include this "submodel" in an integrated population model, so could this submodel using a ZIP just completely use random walk samplers while I use HMC for the submodels without discrete random variables. 

Due to time restrictions, I'm not interested in marginalizing out the bernoulli part for now. 

I'm probably am just misunderstanding something here. Cheers and thanks for any additional insights,
Brian

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: HMC samplers stuck with ZIP
parts:
Dear Brian,
Below are two versions of the example. The first uses the marginalized dZIP and makes it work with AD. Conditionals such as "if(x != 0)" do not work with AD, so it had to be re-written to represent a continuous function of parameters without any if-then-else statements. The type of x also needed to be changed to double(). The second version uses a latent variable for z[i] and works as intended. In both cases one needs to turn on AD via the buildDerivs argument(s). I couldn't exactly follow which case you wanted, but I hope these cover the options and get you started. I realized the example of the web page uses p as probability of a structural zero, whereas often in model code it is flipped to probability of a one (such as presence, or alive, etc). I flipped it in the first example to match what I thought was the natural way to write the second example.
Perry



library(nimble)
library(nimbleHMC)

######
## First version: modify r-nimble example to support AD and HMC
#####

ZIPcode <- nimbleCode({
  p ~ dunif(0,1) # this was probability of absence, but I flipped it...
  lambda ~ dunif(0,10)
  for (i in 1:N)
    y[i] ~ dZIP(lambda, zeroProb = 1-p) # ... to be probability of presence
})

dZIP <- nimbleFunction(
 run = function(x = double(), lambda = double(),
                zeroProb = double(), log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
   returnType(double())
   ## First handle non-zero data
   prob <- zeroProb * dbinom(x, size = 1, prob = 0) + (1 - zeroProb) * dpois(x, lambda)
   if (log) return(log(prob))
   return(prob)
 },
 buildDerivs = 'run'
 )

rZIP <- nimbleFunction(
 run = function(n = integer(), lambda = double(), zeroProb = double()) {
   returnType(double())
   isStructuralZero <- rbinom(1, prob = zeroProb, size = 1)
   if (isStructuralZero) return(0)
   return(rpois(1, lambda))
})

registerDistributions(list(
    dZIP = list(
        BUGSdist = "dZIP(lambda, zeroProb)",
        discrete = TRUE,
        range = c(0, Inf),
        types = c('value = double()', 'lambda = double()', 'zeroProb = double()')
     )))

ZIPmodel <- nimbleModel(ZIPcode, constants = list(N = 100),
                        buildDerivs=TRUE)
ZIPmodel$p <- .6             ## Choose values of p and lambda
ZIPmodel$lambda <- 1.8
set.seed(1)
ZIPmodel$simulate(ZIPmodel$getDependencies(c("p", "lambda"), self=FALSE))       ## Simulate values of y[1]...y[100]
simulatedData <- ZIPmodel$y
simulatedData
ZIPmodel$setData(list(y = simulatedData))  ## Set those values as data in the model
cZIPmodel <- compileNimble(ZIPmodel)

ZIPmcmc <- buildHMC(ZIPmodel)
cZIPmcmc <- compileNimble(ZIPmcmc, project = ZIPmodel)

samples <- runMCMC(cZIPmcmc)
# Per message, the second half are the valid HMC samples
# although in this case they all look similar
summary(samples[5001:10000,])

######
## Second version: use discrete latent state and combination of samplers
#####

ZIPcode2 <- nimbleCode({
  p ~ dunif(0,1)
  lambda ~ dunif(0,10)
  for (i in 1:N) {
    z[i] ~ dbern(p)
    y[i] ~ dpois(lambda*z[i]) ## Note NIMBLE allows R-like named-parameter syntax
  }
})

zData <- rep(1, 100)
boolZero <- simulatedData == 0
zData[ boolZero ] <- NA
zInits <- rep(NA, 100)
zInits[ boolZero ] <- rbinom(sum(boolZero), size = 1, prob = 0.5)

ZIPmodel2 <- nimbleModel(ZIPcode2, constants = list(N = 100),
                         data = list(y = simulatedData, z = zData),
                         inits = list(z = zInits),
                        buildDerivs=TRUE)
cZIPmodel2 <- compileNimble(ZIPmodel2)

ZIPmcmc2 <- buildHMC(ZIPmodel2, monitors = c("lambda", "p", "z"))
cZIPmcmc2 <- compileNimble(ZIPmcmc2, project = ZIPmodel2)

samples2 <- runMCMC(cZIPmcmc2)
summary(samples2[5001:10000,])
